headline: CSET examined whether location verification can enforce AI chip export controls, as Northrop Grumman's YFQ-48A completed its first fully autonomous flight and SIPRI opened enrollment for a WMD non-proliferation course.

points.text: CSET researchers investigated how location verification methods can and cannot improve enforcement of export controls on powerful AI chips, publishing a deep dive on the current state of chip-tracking approaches.
Northrop Grumman's YFQ-48A Collaborative Combat Aircraft completed its first fully autonomous flight, weeks after the US Air Force said it intends to have 500 autonomous aircraft in service by 2032.
SIPRI opened applications for an intensive online course on weapons of mass destruction non-proliferation and disarmament in an era of technological convergence.

SIPRI's Dual-Use and Arms Trade Control Programme delivered a workshop in Canberra on developments in China's export control framework and their implications for Australia and multilateral cooperation.
The UN Tech Envoy's office marked Digital Cooperation Day 2026, pushing to turn Global Digital Compact commitments into action so every country can help shape AI's future rather than just adopt it.

METR research found that while recent AI misalignment incidents show systems capably pursuing goals their supervisors would not approve of, such as hacking other companies, current AI systems still seem relatively bad at concealing misbehavior.
Trump's newly formed 'Super Intelligence' task force faces the challenge of reconciling fiercely divided cabinet factions to forge a coherent AI policy.
A new crop of Western open-weight AI models from Reflection and Mistral is narrowing China's recent lead in open-weight AI, amid industry concern about an AI oligopoly.
